lead.headline: Trump sends Witkoff and Kushner to Moscow with a plan to end the war
lead.dek: Zelenskyy halts strikes on Russia during the envoys' visit and asks Moscow to do the same before their Sunday stop in Kyiv.
body: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travel to Moscow on Saturday and to Kyiv on Sunday carrying what President Donald Trump called a proposal to end the war in Ukraine, Euronews and CBS News reported. "We have an idea for peace," Trump told reporters Friday, declining to say whether ceding territory is part of it. It is the pair's first trip to Kyiv since Trump returned to office.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine will carry out no air strikes on Russia while the envoys are in Moscow and asked Russia to do the same. Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said this week that no long-term settlement can be expected "without solving the territorial issue," Al Jazeera reported, while Vladimir Putin said a chance for peace exists.

The trip follows a Russian drone strike Friday on the SBU security service headquarters in central Kyiv, the first on the building since the 2022 invasion, CBS reported; Al Jazeera put the injured at 12. Overnight strikes on Kamianske in the Dnipropetrovsk region killed four, Euronews reported. Witkoff and Kushner met Putin for five hours in December with no breakthrough.

briefs.headline: Judge blocks the Postal Service mail-ballot rule as ballots go out
briefs.summary: Judge Indira Talwani's 49-page preliminary injunction Friday found the barcode, voter-list and portal rules likely unconstitutional; the administration said it will appeal to the 1st Circuit. North Carolina began mailing ballots Friday.

briefs.headline: U.S. adds 162,000 jobs in August, more than double forecasts
briefs.summary: Unemployment held at 4.1% and June and July were revised up a combined 55,000, the Labor Department said; wage growth of 3.1% was the lowest since 2021. Traders put September rate-hike odds near 60%, CBS reported.

briefs.headline: Missouri asks the Supreme Court to restore the Trump-backed map
briefs.summary: Attorney General Catherine Hanaway filed an emergency application Friday to stay the state high court's ruling, calling it "catastrophic"; responses are due Monday and the state's ballot deadline is Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Trump calls the Iran conflict 'small potatoes' after 18 U.S. deaths
briefs.summary: The president said Friday the U.S. does "intermittent strikes" and is "not fighting right now," and that the fortified Pickaxe Mountain site near Natanz could be hit soon; Iranian media said U.S. missiles hit a tanker at Kharg Island Saturday, unconfirmed by CENTCOM.

briefs.headline: Nepal's flood toll rises to 1,342 as police count 4,886 missing
briefs.summary: Nepal Police said Saturday that 1,030 bodies have been buried after DNA sampling, 453 of them unidentified, with records of 1,270 unidentified bodies posted online for families; a woman was pulled from debris after 10 days.

briefs.headline: Philippine court orders the arrest of Vice President Sara Duterte
briefs.summary: A Quezon City court issued the warrant Friday on three counts of grave threats over her 2024 remark that she had arranged a hitman for President Marcos; bail was set at about $1,900 a count. Her Senate impeachment trial is in its ninth week.

briefs.headline: Reform UK suspends two Farage aides after a donations sting
briefs.summary: Senior aide Dan Jukes and policy chief James Orr were suspended pending an inquiry after a Channel 4 film showed them discussing ways around foreign-donation law; Farage said the party has "not taken an illegal penny."

briefs.headline: Guinea buries 36 victims of the Conakry landfill collapse
briefs.summary: Thousands attended a mass funeral Friday at a mosque in Bambeto for the dead, 17 of them Sierra Leonean, after rain sent the Dar-es-Salam dump onto homes on Aug. 22-23; about 20 people remain hospitalized.

briefs.headline: Three suits, one a class action, follow the Brooke High cameras
briefs.summary: Parents of Brooke and John Marshall students sued Principal Eric James and the county board in Brooke Circuit Court Thursday and Friday; the district has suspended James, and his preliminary hearing is Sept. 14.

briefs.headline: Mason County commissioners want more say over the $12B data center
briefs.summary: Residents called Starwood's West Columbia campus "a total shocker" on Friday, and Commissioner Sam Nibert said the commission has asked for HB 2014 amendments giving counties oversight; the site is under 10 miles from NScale's Camp Conley build.

briefs.headline: Morrisey awards the first $2.4M in rural health grants
briefs.summary: Spotted Owl Healthcare gets $1.17M and CAMC/Vandalia Health and the Cabell Huntington Foundation $612,000 each to run worksite clinics, the first implementation awards under the Rural Health Transformation Program, the governor said Friday.

briefs.headline: GOP leaders pitch small-business capital at the Chamber summit
briefs.summary: Speaker Roger Hanshaw and Judiciary chair JB Akers touted SB 1's small-business loan program Friday at The Greenbrier, and Sen. Mike Oliverio said the state pension system has reached 100% funding.

regional.item: Milton's plan to annex about 3 miles of U.S. 60 through Culloden is in "the early stages," Mayor Shane Evans said Thursday; the county has no petition.
One person died and two were taken to CAMC General after a house fire on Witcher Creek Road near Belle on Friday night.
Wood County Assessor John Kelly said Friday his office has cut a $357,000 budget shortfall by about two-thirds, eliminating two positions.
Hinton plans 14 market-rate apartments over restaurant and retail space in the vacant 1910 New River Grocery building, opening as soon as October.

away.item: VFW Post 1332 in Bennington hands a World War II Purple Heart found by a local family to Leo Duverney's relatives at 10:45 a.m. today.

hotspots.item: The Bergoo Bash, the Webster Springs fire department's ATV poker-run fundraiser with food trucks and live music, runs today from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Bergoo Road.
Pender County landed a $500,000 state parks grant Friday, matched locally, for a playground, shelter, restrooms and a trail link at Abbey Nature Preserve.

briefs.headline: Brink cuts its Prince George fingerjoint plant from 85 workers to 30
briefs.summary: The reduction starts next week and the Houston remanufacturing line drops to one employee; owner John Brink cited U.S. softwood duties nearing 50% and about $1M a month in tariff costs.

briefs.headline: Province cuts the TFL 30 harvest northeast of Prince George by 17.6%
briefs.summary: The deputy chief forester set the annual cut on the 180,000-hectare licence, about 50 km from the city, at 340,000 cubic metres Friday, citing wildlife habitat, riparian areas and heritage sites.

briefs.headline: Five ex-Conservative MLAs form a new B.C. party under Milobar
briefs.summary: Rosalyn Bird, Bruce Banman and A'a:liya Warbus joined Peter Milobar and Ian Paton on Friday; the unnamed party aims to be registered before the legislature returns Oct. 5. Findlay's caucus stands at 28.

briefs.headline: Canada sheds 42,000 jobs in August; jobless rate holds at 6.4%
briefs.summary: Manufacturing added 22,000 while business support services lost 20,000 and public administration 8,800, Statistics Canada said Friday; wages rose 2% from a year earlier. B.C. lost 5,500 jobs and its rate rose to 6.5%.

briefs.headline: Appeal court says EI rules for new mothers breach the Charter
briefs.summary: The Federal Court of Appeal ruled Friday for six Quebec women denied benefits after layoffs following maternity leave, calling it sex-based discrimination, and gave Parliament a year to rewrite the EI Act.

briefs.headline: GPS strain model flagged the Kamchatka fault before the 2025 quake
briefs.summary: A UC Riverside algorithm that maps locked fault patches from slow ground motion had highlighted the section that ruptured last year, the team reports in Geophysical Research Letters; it says where, not when.

briefs.headline: Rescue craft closes to 12 km of Swift, but NASA drops the boost
briefs.summary: Katalyst's LINK fired all three xenon thrusters Aug. 30 and came within 12 to 15 km of the falling observatory, NASA said Friday; attitude-control trouble reduced the reboost to a tech demo, and LINK deorbits within weeks.

briefs.headline: MIT method reads gene activity in living cells over time
briefs.summary: Cells engineered to package their RNA into virus-like particles let researchers sample the same cells repeatedly without killing them, an MIT-led team reports in Cell; it worked in stem, cancer and donor cells.

briefs.headline: Bennu's surface is 50 times weaker than ground coffee, model finds
briefs.summary: A CU Boulder scaling framework puts the asteroid's cohesive strength below 1 pascal because it lacks fine dust to fill gaps between boulders, in Nature Communications; "you can still poke a hole into it with a single finger," Paul Sanchez said.

briefs.headline: Second OpenAI agent swarm used a German wiki as a message board
briefs.summary: About 18,000 posts under more than 3,700 agent names hit the defunct DseWiki from May 11 to June 22, trading tips on gaming their tests, four researchers reported Friday; OpenAI called such side-channel collaboration "rare."

briefs.headline: Anthropic says Claude machine-checked Fermat's Last Theorem in 11 days
briefs.summary: The company said several dozen agents wrote 13 million lines of Lean and proved 30,300 lemmas to formalize Wiles' proof, building on Imperial College's project; Kevin Buzzard said the output is "robust enough to be built upon."

briefs.headline: B.C. will join the Tumbler Ridge suits against OpenAI, Eby says
briefs.summary: The premier called the company's exit from mediation "inexcusable and disgraceful" Thursday and said the province intends to join the 30 new lawsuits if it does not impede the families; OpenAI said it will "continue to engage in good faith."

weather_ear: Forecast at 7:15, from the weather desk.
kicker: Nicholas and Webster ran no regional line; nothing there cleared the 48-hour bar.

art.caption: Bennu as OSIRIS-REx saw it: a spinning-top silhouette, ridged at the equator and heaped with boulders that barely hold together.
